item.title: Generalized particle systems: a locality-factorized metamodel for self-propelled particles and agent-based models
item.description: arXiv:2611.18709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a single formal object, the generalized particle system (GPS), under which self-propelled particle systems (SPPS) and agent-based models (ABMs) are instances of one construction. A GPS is a typed finite population, a per-particle state space with arbitrary internal structure, a global environment, a neighbourhood map that may depend on the configuration, and type-indexed local rules; these assemble into a generator whose iteration is a monoid action, i.e. an autonomous dynamical system. Update schedules and stochastic rules are added at the same generality, so sequential and noisy models (the original Primordial Particle System, Vicsek) are covered, not approximated. The construction isolates the one ingredient separating the two communities: in the classical ABM reading the dependency graph is fixed; in an SPPS it is a function of the state. Under an exchangeability axiom (rules see neighbours only through the multiset of their types and states) the generator is equivariant for type-preserving permutations and descends to a dynamical system on counting measures, the setting of kinetic limits of swarming models. We read the tuple as a metamodel: its structural components coordinatize a space of models inside which numerical parameters live. Six pre-registered experiments on one engine implementing the generator test the claims: freezing the neighbourhood map destroys alignment ($\varphi = 0.91 \to 0.04$) while yielding a different, non-aligned aggregation; the realized neighbourhood graph rewires up to 64% of its edges per step, its rewiring rate anti-correlated with order ($-0.99$); a topological instead of metric neighbourhood reshapes a flocking phase diagram; the same rule with cohesion and separation off shows a Vicsek-type transition whose susceptibility peak grows with system size. One prediction failed and one subsumption claim is unconfirmed; both are reported.
item.dc:creator: Igor Strozzi

item.title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
item.description: arXiv:2611.18752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+\theta}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below. For invariant Gibbs measures associated with H\"older continuous potentials, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity with respect to the defining system and the potential. As an application, we obtain a generic dimension formula: for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, a dense $G_\delta$ set of systems with derivative moduli strictly less than 1/2 has projected dimension equal to the minimum of one and the entropy-to-Lyapunov-exponent ratio.
item.dc:creator: Attila Losonczi

item.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.
item.dc:creator: J. E. Bunder

item.title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
item.description: arXiv:2611.18817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space. As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium. In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
item.description: arXiv:2611.18853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.
item.dc:creator: Vadim A. Kaimanovich

item.title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
item.description: arXiv:2611.18917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula. If, in addition, the splitting is dominated, the dimension formula also implies history independence. The proof first upgrades the measurable fast direction to a holomorphic line field and then uses its invariance on periodic fibers to force the affine product structure. The converse dimension implication combines an entropy comparison argument with rigidity of local symmetries of periodic fiber Julia sets.
item.dc:creator: Yan Mary He

item.title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.18993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the Julia set of the degree-four Fibonacci renormalization 2-periodic point has zero planar Lebesgue measure. As a corollary, the degree four Fibonacci polynomial $z^4+c_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ has zero measure Julia set.
item.dc:creator: Runze Zhang

item.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.19243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Hu

item.title: Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.19478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with B\'ezout degree bounds.
item.dc:creator: Jinxin Xue

item.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.19490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Garrisi, Alessandro Portaluri, Li Wu

item.title: Denoising-Induced Recovery of Effective Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.19516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification. Here, we reveal the effects of filtering, a specific denoising technique, on recovery. Our analysis show that equation discovery performed on filtered data recovers, up to a fixed precision, the normal-form (effective) equations rather than the original system.
item.dc:creator: Narcicegi Kiran

item.title: Word complexity cutoffs for mixing properties of subshifts
item.description: arXiv:2611.19805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Investigating word complexity cutoffs for partial and light mixing in subshifts, we construct partially mixing rank-one subshifts whose word complexity functions $p(q)$ satisfy $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q<2+\epsilon $ for any prescribed $\epsilon>0$ and, conversely, we prove that every lightly mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q>2, $ establishing $2$ as the optimal limiting threshold in the rank-one setting. More quantitatively, we show that every $\alpha$-partially mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q\geq 2+\frac{\alpha}{(1+\alpha)}. $ Our constructions are a combination of staircase and Chacon-like rank-one stages; we introduce the independently interesting notion of mixing spans and meshes to establish partial mixing while retaining low word complexity.
item.dc:creator: Darren Creutz

item.title: Splitting of separatrices in generalized standard maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.19842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider generalized standard maps, that is, maps $F_h:(x,y) \mapsto (x+y+f(x;h),y+f(x;h))$ under quite general assumptions. These maps are area preserving. In particular, the Chirikov standard map, the area preserving H\'enon map and the case $f(x;h)= \varepsilon(x-x^n)$, $n\ge 2$, where $\varepsilon = 4 \sinh^2(h/2)$ satisfy our hypotheses. For all these cases, the problem of the existence of transverse homoclinic points arises. We prove that, for a wide class of generalized standard maps, the primary homoclinic points are transverse, provided that some constant is different from 0.
item.dc:creator: Inmaculada Baldom\'a, D\'idac Gil-Rams, Pau Mart\'in

item.title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Li\'enard systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.19873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Li\'enard system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$, with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$. It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting for $a_2<0$; this system has no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar arcs obtained in potential coordinates. This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).
item.dc:creator: Hebai Chen, Yuhuan Lu, Qian Wang Rui Zhang

item.title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.19874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the polynomial Li\'enard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].
item.dc:creator: Hebai Chen, Jie Jin, Zhijie Li, Jueliang Zhou

item.title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.19880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated. The proof constructs angular minima via quadratic regularization, matching the regularization coefficient to the leading inertial term. A free forcing coefficient allows continuation past bounded accumulations of correction orders. For polynomial potentials, this produces a complete Hahn-series solution, and differential algebraicity gives a common Puiseux denominator. A fixed-denominator continuation estimate together with a finite Taylor transfer extends the construction to analytic potentials. The realization theorem for the resulting invariant formal phase curve then yields a genuine trajectory. We also exhibit an isolated polynomial singularity for which an exact Euler-field identity admits no relatively differentiable solution on the negative set of the potential.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoping Yuan

item.title: Minimal sets of countable group actions on regular curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.19898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimal sets of countable groups acting by homeomorphisms on regular curves. If the ambient action has a finite orbit, every infinite minimal set is an equicontinuous Cantor system. If there is no finite orbit, the minimal set is unique and remains minimal for every finite-index subgroup. A minimal set supporting an invariant probability is a finite orbit, an equicontinuous Cantor system, a circle isometry action, or a Cantor extension obtained by splitting a countable invariant subset of such a circle. Without an invariant probability, infinitely many nondegenerate components can occur. Their homeomorphism types determine the underlying space, and every nonempty countable family of types is realized. The two-generator free group admits an example with arc components on a dendrite, whereas its restricted wreath product with the integers admits none on any regular curve.
item.dc:creator: Enhui Shi, Suhua Wang, Yifei Yu

item.title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.19977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms. Each of the chain transitive sub-systems obtained by Shin can be further decomposed into chain mixing systems by using the ideas of Richeson and Wiseman. Next, we use a probabilistic argument to recover both Smale-like and Bowen-like spectral decompositions for expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. Moreover, we investigate inter-relations among several variants of the shadowing property including the eventual shadowing property, the thick shadowing property, the ergodic shadowing property, the mean ergodic shadowing property and the $M_{\alpha}$-shadowing property.
item.dc:creator: Pramod Kumar Das, Manoj B. Prajapati

item.title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.20055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $\mu$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $\mu$) admit a common minimal model.
item.dc:creator: Yair Hartman, Tomer Zimhoni

item.title: Stability of Carath\'eodory Outer Measures Generated by Spatial Gauges
item.description: arXiv:2611.20104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study outer measures generated by covering costs that depend on both the diameter and the location of a covering set. After establishing the metric and Borel-regularity properties of this construction, we investigate its stability under perturbations of the spatial gauge. For power gauges, we prove a uniform logarithmic criterion: if the exponent perturbation multiplied by $\log(1/r)$ converges uniformly to $\lambda$, then the induced measure is multiplied by $e^{-\lambda}$. Pointwise asymptotic equivalence, however, is insufficient: on $[0,1]$ we construct bounded gauges whose ratio is eventually equal to one at every fixed point, although their induced measures differ by a prescribed factor. In the converse direction, continuity of the ratio in the spatial variable on a Baire space yields equality of the measures on every compact subset of a suitable dense $G_\delta$ set. The results identify a concrete obstruction to pointwise-to-measure stability and a localization principle, while leaving open the corresponding question for all Borel sets.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'e Erlin Castillo, H\'ector Camilo Chaparro

item.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.20303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne Boyd, Jillian Cervantes, Rachel Foster, Olivia Hwang, Sebastian Marcano, Molly Roughan

item.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.20486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.
item.dc:creator: Haoyu Yin, Xudong Chen

item.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.20668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $\theta$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam Edwards, Minju Lee, Hee Oh

item.title: Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.20681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich. For $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, we verify the BMS hypothesis by adapting existing arguments and hence obtain Haar local mixing. As a consequence, we obtain asymptotics for the volume and distribution of long returns and recover the growth indicator from return volumes. Under linear $\theta$-regularity, the transfer also holds with polynomial error estimates. This condition is satisfied by subgroups of $\theta$-Anosov or relatively $\theta$-Anosov groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam Edwards, Minju Lee, Hee Oh

item.title: State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic L\'evy Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.20707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $\alpha$-stable L\'evy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function. We establish invariance of the economically meaningful state space for the discrete reflected model, derive the stationary distribution of the saving target in the Gaussian limiting case, and characterize how the tail index and logistic sensitivity affect the coupled dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations show bimodal capital and saving distributions, asymmetric first-passage behavior between low- and high-capital regimes, and a nonlinear relationship between output volatility, the logistic sensitivity, and the tail index. In particular, heavier tails increase the dispersion of the scaled saving target and low-to-high first-passage frequencies, but do not necessarily increase relative output volatility. The results highlight the importance of state-dependent saving and non-Gaussian shocks for growth dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Wen Wang, Shenglan Yuan

item.title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
item.description: arXiv:2611.20816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $\delta_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/\Lambda$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $\Lambda<G$ is a cocompact lattice; in particular, this applies to finitely generated Zariski-dense semi-groups of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. We also derive a Fourier-analytic criterion for semi-group actions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and use it to prove IC-rigidity for actions arising from suitable matrix-valued polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Fish, Shrey Sanadhya

item.title: Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.20862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=\lambda(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly. Without reaction, it conserves mass, satisfies a discrete maximum principle, and, for $1<p\le 2$, decreases a discrete energy. An example shows that the energy may increase for $p>2$. The truncation error is $O(k+h^2)$ at interior nodes. Numerical tests confirm first order in time and second order in space, and show that the scheme remains positive and bounded for step sizes at which the explicit method breaks down.
item.dc:creator: Achraf Zinihi, Matthias Ehrhardt, Moulay Rchid Sidi Ammi

item.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
item.description: arXiv:2611.20966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $\mu$ and $\mu(f)=0$. The system $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for H\"older observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Matheus M Castro

item.title: The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.21008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Gladkov, Ivan Mitrofanov

item.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.21133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.
item.dc:creator: Are Austad, Christian B\"onicke

item.title: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.21420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit. Under acyclic feeding between its strongly connected components, a max-plus recursion over the reactions gives it; in general neither the Perron root nor the diagonal blocks do. (ii) With one slow species, acyclic feeding and a transversal exit, a fold of the interior critical manifold followed by a drop onto the face gives a unique, exponentially attracting relaxation oscillation whose turning points tend to the fold and exit point. Exactly $3474$ minimal planar networks of molecularity $\leq 3$, with fast per-capita rate affine and decreasing in the slow species, meet our sufficient conditions for it. (iii) A siphon-breaking reaction of rate $\delta$ and finite min-plus breaking order $w$ unfolds the transcritical point into a fold if a Perron-weighted second-order self-interaction is positive, and not if negative; the fold's critical component lies at distance of order $\delta^{w/2}$ from the face. For $\delta=e^{-\mu/^Karepsilon}$ the broken face is a floor at $-\mu$ in the recursion, and planar cycles leave it between the entry-exit and transcritical points, depending on $\mu$. Simulations confirm predicted exits and cycles, including cyclic feeding, where the prediction is conjectural, and high-precision computations confirm the folds; the errors shrink as $^Karepsilon$ or $\delta$ decreases.
item.dc:creator: Miruna-Mihaela Beldiman, Andrei-Dan Halanay

item.title: Cantor Julia sets of positive area in non-autonomous dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.21499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $a>0$, we prove the existence of a sequence of polynomials with rational coefficients whose non-autonomous iteration produces a Julia set of planar area $a$. We also construct a sequence of rational maps with rational coefficients whose Julia set has the same prescribed area. No individual map in this rational sequence is M\"obius-conjugate to a polynomial, and no choice of M\"obius coordinates at successive phases turns it into a polynomial sequence. In both cases, for every $n\geq1$, the Julia set obtained by starting the iteration at the $n$-th map, called the phase-$n$ Julia set, is a Cantor set and meets every neighborhood of each of its points in positive planar area. For every $A\in(0,1)$, we construct two sequences of quadratic polynomials, each with $\infty$ in every phase Julia set and with first phase Julia set of normalized spherical area $A$. In one sequence, every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of locally positive spherical area. In the other, every phase Julia set has countably infinitely many connected components and equals the closure of its interior. Both sequences admit invariant measurable line fields whose essential supports are the corresponding phase Julia sets. Finally, for every $d\in[0,2]$, we construct a sequence of quadratic polynomials for which every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of zero spherical area with local Hausdorff dimension $d$ at each of its points.
item.dc:creator: Lubashan Pathirana

item.title: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.21556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the H\"older continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics. The novelty of our approach allows for the study of such properties notwithstanding the lack of a spectral gap for the corresponding transition operator.
item.dc:creator: Ao Cai, Pedro Duarte, Silvius Klein

item.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.19378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Sinai

item.title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.19571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.
item.dc:creator: Yitong Zhang

item.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2611.19639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network. We identify the dynamical symmetry group of ensembles of Boolean networks that average over random interaction topologies: for networks with $N$ nodes, it is the $N$-dimensional hyperoctahedral group, generated by node-flips and node-label permutations. These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. We also show that input-label permutations constitute a hidden gauge freedom of the dynamics. The Zyklenzeiger symmetry of Boolean functions follows directly from the node-flips of the hyperoctahedral group together with this gauge freedom. Boolean networks related by the hyperoctahedral group have isomorphic state-space networks and form its orbits, and Burnside's lemma gives the number of these orbits for any fixed network topology. It provides a symmetry reduction of the analysis of Boolean network dynamics and explains why the Boolean functions of evolved networks fall into Zyklenzeiger classes, and why these classes split in finite networks.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Kai Mo, Kevin E. Bassler

item.title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.
item.dc:creator: Kang Li, Geng Wang

item.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.20256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by It\^o stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path. Each notion is characterized by a differential condition that is necessary and sufficient for contraction under mild hypotheses. Relations between contraction notions and an associated incremental input-to-state stability result are also established. As an illustration, we apply the established theory to analyze noise-induced synchronization and quantify its robustness with respect to parameter perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Sunghyun Koo, Jin Gyu Lee, Hyungbo Shim

item.title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
item.description: arXiv:2611.20276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific. Maternal and Perinatal Health scored lowest (28.0%), followed by Dental and Oral Health (38.5%) and Behavioral Health (44.4%), while Long-Term Services and Supports (82.8%) and Experience of Care (67.8%) scored highest. State performance correlated strongly with national benchmarks (r = 0.77, approximately), so rates should be read against each measure's benchmark. Domain was the strongest predictor, and the model explained 31.2% of variance. Because of heteroscedasticity and influential observations from mixing bounded and utilization measures, estimates are descriptive. Quality improvement should be targeted by domain, prioritizing maternal health, behavioral health network adequacy, and dental provider participation.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Tesfay, Almaz Abebe

item.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.20344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Vasilyev

item.title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2611.20450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions. In this study, we propose a physics-informed neural network to efficiently calculate the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators. By incorporating three types of loss functions, we train a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to satisfy the governing PDE for the asymptotic phase and the adjoint equation for the phase gradient. The trained network delivers the phase function accurately and, via automatic differentiation, allows the calculation of the phase gradient governing the oscillator's response to perturbations, which enables rapid entrainment closed-loop control using strong inputs. We validate the approach using three types of limit-cycle oscillators and demonstrate that the PINN can facilitate fast and global phase-locking control.
item.dc:creator: Petar Mircheski, Hiroya Nakao

item.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with super critical viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.20638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.
item.dc:creator: Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang

item.title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
item.description: arXiv:2611.21213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.
item.dc:creator: Alain Haraux (LJLL)

item.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.21599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.
item.dc:creator: Brian Yarbrough, Jesse Wayment, Jingbo Wang, Philip E. Par\'{e}, Shreyas Sundaram

item.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
item.description: arXiv:2308.14901v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{\tau_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $\tau_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.
item.dc:creator: Darren Creutz, Ronnie Pavlov

item.title: $C^0$-Contact Anosov flows
item.description: arXiv:2503.00454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that smooth reparametrizations of the geodesic flow on a manifold of constant negative curvature are contact Anosov flows. In particular we give a new class of exponentially mixing Anosov flows. Moreover, this introduces the notion of $C^0$-contact and we prove that the classical Gray stability theorem that is known in the smooth case fails in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Cheikh Khoule, Matheus Manso, Ameth Ndiaye, Khadim War

item.title: On the future cover of a sofic shift
item.description: arXiv:2512.01368v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper contains a new proof of the theorem by Krieger which establishes the canonicity of the future cover of a sofic shift. In addition the paper describes a method to produce new canonical covers from a given one, resulting in canonical covers related to, but generally different from the future cover.
item.dc:creator: Klaus Thomsen

item.title: The Narrow Corridor of Stable Solutions in an Extended Osipov--Lanchester Model with Constant Total Population
item.description: arXiv:2512.18515v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies a modification of the classical Osipov-Lanchester model in which the total population of the two sides, $N=R+B$, stays constant. In this model the ratio $y=R/B$ obeys the Riccati equation $\dot y=\alpha y^2-\beta$, which is solvable in elementary functions for all values of the parameters. The main result is a complete classification of the stable regimes. An asymptotically stable invariant set in the quadrant $R,B\ge 0$ exists only in three cases: $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ gives a stable interior equilibrium; $\alpha=0,\ \beta<0$ makes the boundary $B=0$ stable; $\alpha<0,\ \beta=0$ makes the boundary $R=0$ stable. If $\alpha>0$ or $\beta>0$, every solution except one unstable equilibrium reaches a boundary of the quadrant in finite time, where the model stops being applicable. If the parameters vary in time, a fixed distance from the boundaries is kept when $\alpha(t)$ and $\beta(t)$ obey buffer dynamics that push them away from zero. Finally, in the case $\alpha<0,\ \beta<0$ the original system grows exponentially, while in the two degenerate cases it grows at most linearly. Growth demanded of a given cost, the sum of the two channels, bounds their imbalance and, with the perturbation bound, confines the parameters to an explicit wedge about $|\alpha|=|\beta|$ truncated near the origin: the narrow corridor of the model.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Salishev

item.title: Function-on-function nonlinear autoregressive model (F2NARX) for probabilistic surrogate modeling of stochastic dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2602.01929v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally efficient surrogate models for predicting dynamical system responses is critical in many engineering domains, yet remains challenging due to the strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional mapping from external excitations and system parameters to system responses. This work introduces a novel Function-on-Function Nonlinear AutoRegressive model with eXogenous inputs (F2NARX), which reformulates the recently proposed $\mathcal{F}$-NARX method from a function-on-function regression perspective. The proposed framework substantially improves predictive efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. By combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression, F2NARX further enables probabilistic predictions of dynamical responses via the unscented transform in an autoregressive manner. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through case studies of varying complexity. Results show that F2NARX outperforms state-of-the-art NARX model by orders of magnitude in efficiency while achieving higher accuracy in general. The probabilistic prediction capability of F2NARX is further demonstrated by combining it with active learning for first-passage probability estimation, showing its potential for reliability-oriented applications.
item.dc:creator: Zhouzhou Song, Marcos A. Valdebenito, Styfen Sch\"ar, Stefano Marelli, Bruno Sudret, Matthias G. R. Faes

item.title: Three heteroclinic orbits induce a countable family of equivalence classes of regular flows
item.description: arXiv:2603.07470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the problem of topological classification for smooth structurally stable flows on closed four-dimensional manifolds, the non-wandering set of which contains exactly two saddle equilibria, and the wandering set contains isolated trajectories connecting these saddle equilibria (heteroclinic curves). In particular, we show that for a flow of the class under consideration on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, the number of heteroclinic curves is a complete topological invariant, while on the sphere $\mathbb S^4$, there exists a countably many equivalence classes with an arbitrary odd number $\gamma\geq 3$ of heteroclinic curves. These results contrast with a three-dimensional case, where under similar conditions there exists only finite set of equivalence classes for each number of heteroclinic curves.
item.dc:creator: Elena Gurevich

item.title: On the Rokhlin lemma for infinite measure-preserving bijections
item.description: arXiv:2604.13802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Rokhlin lemma in the context of infinite measure-preserving bijections, and completely classify such bijections up to $\lambda$-approximate conjugacy, where $\lambda$ is the infinite measure which is preserved. This sharpens considerably the classical version of the Rokhlin lemma, which provides such a classification up to $\mu$-approximate conjugacy where $\mu$ is a probability measure equivalent to $\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Fabien Hoareau, Fran\c{c}ois Le Ma\^itre

item.title: Reentrant value fields as delayed coupled reaction-diffusion systems on finite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.03940v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a dynamical system in which a symbolic field is coupled to a geometric field via a bipartite Hilbert-Schmidt kernel. The system is fully described by a retarded functional differential equation (RFDE) on the history space, subject to Lipschitz and small gain conditions. We show that the RFDE is well-posed under constant input and that it admits a compact global attractor. The principal subsystem $(H_L, X_R, P)$, which is comprised of the two primary fields as well as an executive field, is shown to be globally stable independent of delay, provided that the interfield coupling satisfies $C_{\mathcal{K}}^2<\mu_L\mu_R$. In addition, we describe design specifications that fulfill the hypotheses of the main Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Karsten Bohlen

item.title: Rigidity and equidistribution of random walks by diffeomorphisms near the conservative regime
item.description: arXiv:2605.27008v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a random walk on a closed manifold $M$ driven by a probability measure $\mu$ on the set of $C^2$-diffeomorphisms. Provided $\mu$ has compact support, satisfies certain gap, pinching, and ergodicity conditions, and is weak-$*$ close to volume-preserving, we prove $M$ carries exactly one atom-free stationary probability measure $\Upsilon_{\mu}$. It has finite high-dimensional Riesz energy and coincides with volume in the volume-preserving setting. Moreover, for every $x\in M$, the $n$-step distribution $\mu^{*n}*\delta_{x}$ converges to $\Upsilon_{\mu}$ unless $x$ is trapped in a finite $\mu$-invariant set. Our result applies to a variety of situations: bi-expanding random walks on surfaces, non-linear perturbations of Zariski-dense random walks on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, on cocompact lattice quotients of $\mathrm{SO}(2,1), \mathrm{SO}(3,1)$, or on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'ee B\'enard, Zhiyuan Zhang

item.title: A Structural Theory of Admissible Transitions in Biological Reaction Networks
item.description: arXiv:2608.27201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Biological reaction networks exhibit transient changes that cannot be understood from steady states or long-term persistence alone. We extend Chemical Organization Theory to transitions between species subsets, using stoichiometry and feasible reaction fluxes to characterize structurally admissible changes without specifying kinetic parameters. The framework distinguishes algebraic admissibility from feasibility constrained by reactant availability. We relate these transitions to reaction-based ordinary differential equations and identify an asymmetry: closure-building transitions are determined by network structure, whereas subsequent reductions can depend on the realized trajectory. Transitions to terminal organizations are characterized when the relevant species sets occur along that trajectory. An HIV-immune response model illustrates how a shared closure-building phase can precede different long-term outcomes. The framework connects continuous dynamics with discrete changes in species composition and supports structural analysis of transient pathways and organization formation in systems biology, while distinguishing structural admissibility from realization under particular kinetics.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Peter, Bashar Ibrahim

item.title: A finite Livshits theorem and local length spectrum rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2609.23762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for closed negatively curved Riemannian manifolds whose length spectrum is exponentially separated, the length spectrum is a local isometry invariant. The main tool used in the proof is a finitary version of the Livshits theorem with an exponential tail that improves with the regularity.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan DeWitt, Spencer Durham, James Marshall Reber, Thomas Aloysius O'Hare

item.title: Common invariant measures for beta-transformations: affine relations and squared bases
item.description: arXiv:2609.31156v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the common invariant probabilities of two beta-transformations in two families. In the first, the bases satisfy $\gamma=a\beta+c>1$ with $\beta>1$ irrational, $a,c\in\mathbb Q$ and $a+c\ne1$. In the second, they are an irrational $\beta>1$ and its square. In both families every common singular invariant probability is the point mass at zero; combining this with the classification of coincident R\'enyi--Parry measures gives all common invariant probabilities, with no entropy, ergodicity or multiplicative-independence hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Hang Zhao

item.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.33250v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Wang, Guowei Yu

item.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
item.description: arXiv:2610.24848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$ of rotation numbers. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotation numbers in $I$ is an ellipse. It suffices to assume these caustics at a suitably chosen family of rotation numbers in $I$ with any prescribed rational point of $I$ as its unique accumulation point. The key linear result classifies real $L^2$ displacements with phase-independent orbit sums at every rational rotation number in $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.
item.dc:creator: Guan Huang

item.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
item.description: arXiv:2610.32820v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider an attractor $\Lambda$ of a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbf M^d$ with a trapping neighborhood $U$ and an extendable continuous invariant splitting $T_{\overline U}\mathbf M^d=E\oplus F$. Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures on $\Lambda$ that satisfy Pesin's entropy formula and have negative Lyapunov exponents on $E$ and positive exponents on $F$. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures, and the corresponding sets of asymptotically hyperbolic points are covered, modulo Lebesgue null sets, by the basins of at most countably many such measures. We give necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of ergodic SRB measures with these exponent signs in terms of derivative growth and orbit statistics, and characterize the relationship between physical measures, strongly observable measures, physical-like measures and such SRB measures. We also construct examples with unique hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Bai, Wanshan Lin, Xueting Tian

item.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.33218v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists. We apply these results to matrix cocycles, establishing the existence of invariant measures that realize the joint spectral radius for countable families of matrices.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Juliano S. Gonschorowski

item.title: Magnetic billiards: duality and magnetic Radon property
item.description: arXiv:2610.33782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.
item.dc:creator: Michael (Misha), Bialy

item.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39907v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Thorat

item.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
item.description: arXiv:2610.40147v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood Latt\`es phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating; that is, we show that a positive bifurcation (1,1)-current implies positivity of the associated bifurcation measure on the parameter space. Working over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we characterize arithmetic and geometric potential bigness for the canonical line bundle associated to families of endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ when restricted to the subvarieties. As consequences, we obtain uniform bounds for the periods and preperiods of relations among non-exceptional maps, and we show uniform bounds on the geometry of preperiodic points satisfying these relations. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, our results yield corresponding uniform bounds for points and subvarieties satisfying a height gap.
item.dc:creator: Laura DeMarco, Niki Myrto Mavraki

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09066v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.
item.dc:creator: Antti K\"aenm\"aki, R. D\'aniel Prokaj, K\'aroly Simon, Sascha Troscheit

item.title: Complement Cancellation and the Spectral Characterization of Three-Point Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2611.09143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate both two-sided and one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence within the framework of weakly mixing measure-preserving systems. As our principal result, we establish an exact spectral characterization for the failure of two-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence: namely, a subset \(R\subseteq\mathbb N\) fails to possess this property if and only if there exist a continuous symmetric probability measure \(\sigma\) on \(\mathbb T\) and a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying \[ 2\widehat{\sigma}(n)+\widehat{\sigma}(2n)\leq-\varepsilon \qquad(n\in R). \] Our proof of the necessity relies upon a complement-symmetrized correlation identity, whereas the converse is achieved through a construction involving a stationary Gaussian system, a bounded odd observable, Hermite expansions, and an independent Bernoulli extension. Furthermore, we extend this characterization to three-point polynomial configurations as well as to actions of countable abelian groups. In addition, we derive an unconditional analogue in which arbitrary symmetric probability measures take the place of continuous ones, thereby demonstrating a strict separation between the ergodic and weakly mixing classes of recurrence. Subsequently, we turn our attention to the distinction between two-sided and ordinary one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence. It is shown that a suitable negative spectral condition compels the failure of one-sided recurrence. More remarkably, we construct an explicit weakly mixing system wherein the quadratic spectral expression remains uniformly positive, yet the presence of a negative cubic correlation still induces a one-sided recurrence deficit. Consequently, it follows that two-point spectral data alone are insufficient to govern one-sided \(2\)-nice recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Dibyendu De

item.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
item.description: arXiv:2307.13191v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.
item.dc:creator: Bin Pei, Robert Hesse, Bjoern Schmalfuss, Yong Xu

item.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
item.description: arXiv:2501.12763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether \[ S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}} \] converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erd\H{o}s and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].
item.dc:creator: Lorenz Fruehwirth, Manuel Hauke-Treuer

item.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
item.description: arXiv:2510.04419v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $\nu\neq\kappa$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally. Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.
item.dc:creator: Jihao Liu, Zheng Xu

item.title: Length Spectrum Rigidity and Flexibility of Spheres of Revolution with One Equator
item.description: arXiv:2601.16804v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a notion of marked length spectrum for $S^1$-symmetric Riemannian metrics on the two-sphere having only one equator. We prove that isospectral metrics in this class have conjugate geodesic flows. Under a further ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetry assumption, we show that the marked length spectrum determines the metric. Finally, we show that every isospectral class of metrics contains a unique ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetric metric and give an explicit description of this isospectral class as an infinite-dimensional convex set, generalizing the known description of $S^1$-symmetric Zoll metrics. This paper contains also two appendices, in which we provide an elementary proof of the fact that a $C^2$ real-valued function on an interval is determined by the set of tangent lines to its graph, and we classify a class of $S^1$-invariant contact forms on three-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Abbondandolo, Marco Mazzucchelli

item.title: A superposition approach for the ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem with pointwise dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2603.15346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For nonlinear time-delay systems, we show that the existence of a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) with pointwise dissipation (i.e., dissipation in terms of the current solution norm) suffices for input-to-state stability, provided that uniform global stability can also be ensured using the same LKF. To this end, we employ elements of a recently developed stability theory in which the behavior of solutions is not assessed through the classical norm but rather through a specific LKF. As a consequence of our results, we obtain a strengthening and extension of the classical Lyapunov-Krasovskii theorem for undisturbed systems to systems with uniformly bounded disturbances. We discuss the advantages of our approach by means of an example.
item.dc:creator: Andrii Mironchenko, Fabian Wirth, Antoine Chaillet, Lucas Brivadis

item.title: Structure-Aware Tensorial Model Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2604.26280v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work investigates a two-stage method for constructing projection-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs). Based on established tensorial ROM methodology, the proposed approach reduces dimensionality offline by encoding solution snapshots using a multi-linear Tucker factorization, so that a reduced basis which varies nonlinearly with PDE parameters can be rapidly constructed online and used in a Galerkin ROM. Two novel extensions of this strategy, tailored to the cases of structured PDEs and sparse parameter sampling, are presented: the construction of reduced bases orthonormalized with respect to a general discrete inner product, and the interpolation of encoded states via radial basis functions. Basic representation and ROM error estimates are presented demonstrating the validity of these modifications, and the approach is challenged on state-linear examples where monolithic-basis ROMs are known to struggle, including a realistic instance of Maxwell's equations in 3D. Results suggest that the proposed nonlinear basis ROM can effectively mitigate linear restrictions on Kolmogorov $n$-width while improving upon previous tensorial ROM technology, particularly in the highly nonlinear and data-limited regimes characteristic of practical use cases.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Vijaywargiya, Eric C. Cyr, Anthony Gruber

item.title: Structural functional identifiability and model discovery in differential equation models
item.description: arXiv:2606.30289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Differential equation models are widely used to describe, interpret, and predict dynamical phenomena across science and engineering. In practice, however, the governing dynamics are rarely fully known and must be inferred from observational data. Traditionally, inverse problems in differential equation modelling have focused on estimating unknown parameter values. In this setting, structural identifiability determines whether parameter values can, in principle, be uniquely recovered from ideal observations and is, therefore, a prerequisite for meaningful inference. More recently, the integration of machine learning with mechanistic modelling has enabled the discovery of unknown equations, functions, and constitutive relationships, substantially expanding the space of admissible models. This raises a fundamental question: under what conditions can unknown functional components be uniquely recovered from data? In this paper, we generalise the classical notion of structural parameter identifiability to functional identifiability. We first identify broad classes of models for which unique functional recovery is impossible.
