We then show how functional identifiability can be assessed for differential equation models using differential algebra-based techniques which are well-established as a means of assessing structural identifiability for ordinary differential equation models. Our framework reveals new phenomena that arise in the transition from parametric to function inference and have no analogue in the classical setting. Finally, we characterise functional identifiability in several common model classes. Taken together, our results demonstrate that functional identifiability provides a theoretical foundation for modern inverse problems in differential equation modelling, particularly those that use machine learning representations of unknown system components.
item.dc:creator: Torkel E Loman, Alexander P Browning, Ruth E Baker

item.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
item.description: arXiv:2607.12995v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3214 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.481e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic points of the circle. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.
item.dc:creator: Avner Kantor

item.title: Boundary Collisions and Weak Excitation in LQR Policy-Gradient Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.00297v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Closed-loop stability concerns all initial states, whereas an LQR cost evaluates only the directions excited by a prescribed initial-state distribution. We study how this distinction affects Euclidean policy-gradient flows. For every nonzero deficient covariance rank, we construct relatively open families of controllable data and open sets of stabilizing initial gains whose exact gradient trajectories reach the stability boundary in finite optimization time. The state Gramian can remain positive definite at every time before collision. By separating the cost contribution of a critical mode, we obtain a local collision criterion based on direction attraction and motion toward the stability boundary. Adding excitation of strength $\varepsilon$ yields matching $\Theta(\sqrt\varepsilon)$ bounds on the local minimum stability margin for trajectories that would otherwise collide. For a class of single-input, corank-one systems, these bounds hold over the entire trajectory without a common compact-set assumption. Numerical examples further illustrate the dynamics and scaling laws.
item.dc:creator: Kang Liu

item.title: Inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson structures from vector field samples
item.description: arXiv:2610.04350v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a method for the data-driven inference of Hamiltonian and Lie-Poisson dynamical systems from vector-field samples, in which the Hamiltonian and the underlying Poisson tensor are estimated jointly rather than assuming the structure is known. The Hamiltonian is represented as a linear combination of random feature maps with fixed random internal weights, so its estimation is a linear regression problem for any given Poisson structure. We treat three cases of increasing generality: a known Poisson tensor, an unknown constant invertible (symplectic) structure matrix, and Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson structures, with structure matrix linear in the state. In the constant case, the Hamiltonian and structure matrix are recovered jointly from an eigenvalue problem that avoids the trivial zero solution due to the scaling symmetry of Hamiltonian systems. For Lie-Poisson and affine Poisson systems we alternate between an initial Hamiltonian estimate from a generalized eigenvalue problem for an approximate first integral, and a constrained nonlinear least-squares fit of the structure constants that enforces the Jacobi identity and, for affine structures, the cocycle condition, via continuation in a penalty parameter. Orthogonal matching pursuit selects a compact, well-conditioned subset of random features. Because the learned Hamiltonian is a sum of single-feature terms, the model admits an explicit Poisson/symplectic splitting integrator, which we use to validate the learned systems via long-time Poincare sections. We demonstrate the approach on the four- and five-dimensional Lorenz-86 model and a six-dimensional Kirchhoff rigid-body system, recovering Hamiltonians, structure constants and Casimir invariants to high accuracy, and showing the inferred Poincare sections converge to the correct invariant-tori topology as the number of random features increases.
item.dc:creator: Jason E. Frank, Georg A. Gottwald

item.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.28026v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez

item.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
item.description: arXiv:2611.02535v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be induced by a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.
item.dc:creator: Morgan O'Brien

item.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.03514v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Runze Zhang

item.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.17813v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Wen Jiang, Hao Luo
